title: Build the endless gathering game you saw in ads
summary: A former web designer who had never made a game wrote the story while Codex built Point Nemo, refining it through repeated play-and-feedback rounds.
agent_role: Codex wrote and rebuilt the game code. The human wrote the story, played each version and gave feedback.
outcome: The author reports finishing a polished game called Point Nemo.
what_they_did: The poster, a web designer who had just closed their company, wanted the kind of game seen in mobile ads: gather things, sell them, expand your facilities forever. They had never made a game. They wrote the story, Codex built a version, they played it, then gave feedback for the next round.
how_it_went: They say the build-play-feedback loop produced a polished game called Point Nemo.
worth_knowing: The human's job was story and play-testing, not coding. Repeated short rounds of play and feedback did the polishing.
prompt: Help me build a simple browser game where the player gathers [resource], sells it, and spends the money to expand [facilities] in an endless loop. Here is the story and setting: [your story]. Start with a small playable version, tell me how to run it, and wait for my feedback after I play it. Then improve it one round at a time based on what I say.

curation.rationale: A non-programmer built a full idle-style game with Codex by writing the story and play-testing each build. It is a genuine agent build loop, but the post gives few details and no numbers.
